evals.prompt: Parse this Figma node URL and tell me the file key and API node id: https://www.figma.com/design/AbCdEf1234567890/My-App?node-id=12-34&t=abc
evals.expected_output: Identifies file_key AbCdEf1234567890 and node_id 12:34, noting conversion from URL hyphen form to API colon form.

evals.prompt: Using evals/files/sample-figma-file.json, summarize the pages, main frames, colors, and text styles.
evals.expected_output: Runs the summarize/tokens commands on local JSON and reports the Home page, Checkout frame, component/style counts, color candidates, and typography candidates.

evals.prompt: I only care about node 45:67 in this Figma file. What should you fetch first?
evals.expected_output: Recommends GET /v1/files/:key/nodes with ids=45:67 and shallow depth before fetching more deeply, not a full unbounded file read.

evals.prompt: Using evals/files/sample-figma-file.json, find any nodes whose name matches 'button|cta|checkout' across FRAME, COMPONENT, INSTANCE, and TEXT types.
evals.expected_output: Runs `scripts/figma_read.py find evals/files/sample-figma-file.json --name 'button|cta|checkout' --types FRAME COMPONENT INSTANCE TEXT` and reports the matching node ids, names, and types.

evals.prompt: I tried to fetch a private Figma file and got a 403, and I have not set FIGMA_TOKEN. How should I proceed?
evals.expected_output: Explains that 403 typically means the token is missing, expired, lacks scopes, or lacks file access; instructs the user to export FIGMA_TOKEN (or FIGMA_OAUTH_TOKEN for bearer) with at least file_content:read; notes that --auth auto picks X-Figma-Token for FIGMA_TOKEN and Bearer for FIGMA_OAUTH_TOKEN; warns not to paste tokens in prompts.
